The great market that gathered at Mecca each year around the Hajj, the pilgrimage every Muslim who can afford it should make once in life. Pilgrims came to pray, but many also came to trade, which made it the largest fair in the Islamic world.

The Quran allows trade during the pilgrimage, and before Islam fairs were held near Mecca in the sacred months. The chart's date, 1184, is when the Andalusian traveller Ibn Jubayr described the Mecca market, piled with goods from India, Iraq, Yemen and Ethiopia, saying the products of the whole world could be found there.

Great caravans set out each year from Cairo and Damascus, and ships landed pilgrims at Jeddah. Rulers used the journey to show their wealth, as on Mansa Musa's pilgrimage in 1324. Merchants across the Muslim world timed their debts and deals to the pilgrimage calendar. Ideas moved too: scholars met, books changed hands, and coffee spread from Yemen with pilgrims. Travellers such as Ibn Battuta began their journeys on the Hajj.
